texts.facts: 1. The appellant is aggrieved by the impugned judgment dated 16/12/2017 of Ld. MM-02, South-East District, Saket Courts, vide which he was convicted for offence U/s. 279/304A IPC and by order on sentence dated 06/01/2018 vide which he was sentenced to undergo Simple Rajbir vs The State on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135484284/ 1 Imprisonment of two years alongwith fine of Rs.5,000/- for offence U/s. 304A IPC. He was sentenced to undergo Simple Imprisonment of six months for offence U/s. 279 IPC, in case FIR No. 778/2007, PS Okhla Industrial Area, U/s. 279/304A IPC. Both the sentences were directed to run concurrently. 2. The prosecution case in brief is that on 18/09/2007, at about 08:00AM, opposite D-3, adjacent to wall of FCI Go-down, Tehkhand, Okhla Industrial Area, accused Rajbir while driving Truck No. HR-38N-3215 in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others, hit victim girl Pratibha @ Priya, aged 04 years, a pedestrian who was going to market with her father, and crushed her under the left side front wheel of the truck. Accused/appellant Rajbir was arrested on the same day of incident for causing death of victim girl Pratibha @ Priya by rash or negligent act, not amounting to culpable homicide. On completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed for the offence U/s. 279/304A IPC. Notice U/s. 251 CrPC for offence U/s. 279/304A IPC was served upon the accused, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 3. As per Trial Court record, to prove its case, the prosecution examined following 09 witnesses during trial of the case: (i) PW1/complainant Ajay Kumar Rai, father of deceased/victim girl, deposed that on 18/09/2007, at about 08:00AM, he alongwith her daughter Pratibha @ Priya, aged 04 years, was going to purchase vegetable from Tehkhand and, while walking on side of the road, when they reached opposite D-3, FCI go-down, one truck bearing registration number HR- 38N-3215, being driven by its driver in zigzag manner and fast speed, came from their behind and its left front tyre ran over his daughter. He deposed that public persons apprehended the driver of offending truck at the spot and battered him. Someone called police at 100 number, on which PCR took his daughter and the accused driver to hospital. He deposed that police met him at the spot and recorded his statement Ex. PW1/A. He deposed that he went to AIIMS Hospital, where he met the accused, who was arrested vide arrest memo Ex. PW1/B and his personal search was conducted vide memo Ex. PW1/C. After postmortem examination, body of his daughter was handed over to him, through identification memo Ex. PW1/D. (ii) PW2 ASI Ram Avtar, Duty Officer, deposed about registration of FIR Ex. PW2/A on the basis of rukka that he received from Ct. Virender on 18/09/2007. (iii) PW3 Taslimuddin Siddiqui conducted mechanical inspection of Eicher Truck bearing Registration No. HR-38N- 3215 on 18/09/2007 and proved his detailed report Ex. PW3/A. (iv) PW4 HC Virender Singh deposed that on 18/09/2007, at about 08:37AM, on receipt of DD No.2A regarding accident by SI Shyam Sunder, both of them reached the spot i.e. Tehkhand Road, D-3, opposite FCI go-down, Okhla Industrial Area, where they found standing one Truck bearing registration No. HR-38N- 3215 in accidental condition. He deposed that on receipt of another DD No.6A at the spot from Ct. Vinod regarding admission of injured in AIIMS Hospital, he alongwith Rajbir vs The State on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135484284/ 2 the IO reached AIIMS, where IO obtained MLC of deceased victim girl Priya, aged 04 years, on which the concerned doctor made endorsement that the patient was brought dead. He stated that Ajay Kumar, father of deceased girl, and one other person Kailash met him in hospital, who handed driver Rajbir i.e. accused/appellant to him. He further deposed about recording of statement of father of deceased girl, registration of FIR, arrest as well as personal search of the accused, hading over of dead body to its relatives, preparation of site plan at the instance of complainant, seizure of offending truck and depositing the case property in Malkhana. (v) PW5 Ct. Vinod deposed that on 18/09/2010 on receipt of DD No.6A regarding accident at D-3 (supra), he reached the spot of incident and handed over the said DD to IO SI Shyam Sunder. (vi) PW6 HC Jagram deposed that on 18/09/2007 he was posted as In-charge/HC at PCR Eagle-33 and, at about 08:00AM, on receipt of information regarding accident near red light, the exact location of which he did not remember, he reached the spot and found that a truck, registration number of which he did not remember, was standing there. He deposed that one girl alongwith her father, public persons and truck driver Rajbir were present at the spot. He deposed that the accused driver was handed over to the IO, whereas, the girl was rushed to AIIMS Hospital, where she was declared dead. Since PW6 did not disclose the complete facts, he was cross examined by Ld. APP. In cross-examination by Ld. APP, PW6 admitted that the spot of incident was opposite D-3, FCI go-down, Okhla Industrial Area, New Delhi, and the registration number of the offending vehicle was HR-38N-3215. (vii) PW7 Dinesh Kumar, Medical Record Technician, AIIMS Hospital, identified the handwriting and signature of Dr. Sushil Sharma, who prepared Postmortem Report No. 1237/07 dated 18/09/2007 Ex. PW7/A of deceased victim girl Pratibha @ Priya, bearing signature of Dr. Sushil at point 'A'. (viii) PW8 Brij Gopal was registered owner of the offending Truck bearing registration No. HR-38N-1532, who got it released from the Court. (ix) PW9 Aji Singh, Record Clerk, AIIMS, identified the handwriting and signature of Dr. Ajay Kumar, who prepared MLC No.17967 dated 18/09/2007 Ex. PW9/A of injured Priya. 4. Statement of accused Rajbir was recorded U/s. 313 CrPC. He denied all incriminating evidence and asserted that he was falsely implicated in the case. He asserted that he did not cause any accident; neither was he driving the truck at the time of accident. He stated that his truck was stationed and he was sleeping on its roof. He asserted that some another vehicle hit the deceased and fled from the spot with the offending vehicle. He led no evidence in defence. 5. Upon hearing the final arguments from both sides, Ld. Trial Court vide its judgment dated 16/12/2017 held the appellant/accused guilty of offence U/s. 279/304A IPC and sentenced him vide order on sentence dated 06/01/2018. Rajbir vs The State on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135484284/ 3 6. Ld. Counsel for appellant vehemently argued that Ld. Trial Court passed the impugned judgment on surmises and conjectures. The appellant prayed for setting aside of his conviction and for acquittal of the offence U/s. 279/304A IPC. 7. Ld. Addl. PP for State/respondent has opposed the appeal stating that prosecution proved its case against the appellant and Ld. Trial Court rightly convicted and sentenced him. 9. PW1 Ajay Kumar is father of the victim girl. He deposed that on 18/09/2007 he and his daughter Pratibha @ Priya, aged04 years, were going on foot to buy vegetables from Tehkhand at about 08:00AM. When they reached opposite D-3, FCI Go- down, and were walking on side of the road, one Truck bearing registration no. HR-38N-3215 being driven by accused Rajbir (appellant herein) in a zigzag manner and at a fast speed, came from back side and crushed his daughter under left front tyre of his truck. The accused was apprehended at the spot and battered by the public persons. Someone from public called PCR. The PCR took his daughter and the accused to hospital. His statement Ex. PW1/A was recorded by police at the spot. Thereupon, PW1 went to AIIMS Hospital, where appellant/accused was present and postmortem examination of his deceased daughter was conducted. In cross-examination, PW1 replied that at the time of accident no other truck was present at the spot. He replied that police recorded his statement at the spot at about 08:15AM. The version of PW1 is corroborated by PW3 Taslimuddin Siddiqui, who conducted mechanical inspection of the Eicher Truck No. HR-38N-3215. As per his report Ex. PW3/A, left side corner bumper plastic ear was found pressed and front grill of the truck was found damaged. 10. It is not in dispute that the offending Truck No. HR-38N- 3215 of the accused was found stationed by PW6 HC Jagram when he reached in his PCR Eagle-33 police van at the spot on receiving the information of accident, 18/09/2007 at 08:00AM. He deposed that he found injured girl and his father at the spot. The truck diver i.e. accused Rajbir was also present at the spot and he was handed over to IO. The injured girl child was rushed to AIIMS Hospital where she was declared dead. 11. Ld. Counsel for appellant argued that PW1 Ajay Kumar was interested witness and he falsely implicated appellant Rajbir for the accident, although, PW1 was not present at the spot at the time of accident. Secondly, PW6 HC Jagram, In-charge of PCR Van that reached the spot immediately after the incident, deposed that injured girl child, her father as well as offender truck driver were found present at the spot. PW1 was not known to the appellant and he had no motive to falsely implicate him for the road accident.
texts.arguments: On the other hand, Ld. Addl. PP rightly argued that victim child was only 04 years old and there is no reasonable doubt that she was accompanied by her father i.e. PW1 Ajay Kumar.

Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in Ravi Kapur Vs. State of Rajasthan (2012) 9 SCC 284 that -
12.Rash and negligent driving has to be examined in the light of facts and circumstances of a given case.
It is a fact incapable of being construed or seen in isolation.
It must be examined in the light of attended circumstances.
A person who drives a vehicle on the road is liable to be held responsible for the act as well as for the result.
It may not be always possible to determine with reference to the speed of a vehicle whether a person was driving rashly and negligently.
Both these acts presuppose an abnormal conduct.
Even when one is driving a vehicle at a slow speed but recklessly and negligently, it would amount to "rash and negligent driving" within the meaning of language of Section 279 IPC.
That is why the Legislature in its wisdom has used the words "manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life".

The preliminary condition, thus, are that - (a) it is the manner in which the vehicle is driven; (b) it be driven either rashly or negligently; and (c) such rash or negligent driving should be such as to endanger human life.
Once these ingredients are satisfied, the penalty contemplated under Section 279 IPC is attracted.

13.'Negligence' means omission to do something which a reasonable and prudent person guided by the considerations which ordinary regulate human affairs would do or doing something which a prudent and reasonable person guided by similar con
Negligence is not an absolute term but is a relative one; it is rather a comparative term.
It is difficult to state with precision any mathematically exact formula by which negligence or lack of it can be infallibly measured in a given case.

Whether there exists negligence per se or the course of conduct amounts to negligence will normally depend upon the attending and surrounding facts and circumstances which have to be taken into consideration by the Court.
In a given case, even not doing what one was ought to do can constitute negligence.
14.The Court has to adopt another parameter i.e. 'reasonable care' in determining the question of negligence or contributory negligence.

The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation or a duty upon a person (for example a driver) to care for the pedestrian on the road and this duty attains a higher degree when the pedestrians happen to be children of tender years.

It is axiomatic to say that while driving a vehicle on a public way, there is an implicit duty cast on the drivers to see that their driving does not endanger the life of the right users of the road, may be either vehicular users or pedestr
They are expected to take sufficient care to avoid danger to others.
15.The other principle that is pressed in aid by the courts in such cases is the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur.

This doctrine serves two purposes - one that an accident may by its nature be more consistent with its being caused by negligence for which the opposite party is responsible than by any other causes and that in such a case, the mere fact of
Secondly, it is to avoid hardship in cases where the claimant is able to prove the accident but cannot prove how the accident occurred.
The courts have also applied the principle of res ipsa loquitur in cases where no direct evidence was brought on record.
The Act itself contains a provision which concerns with the consequences of driving vehicle dangerously alike the provision in the IPC that the vehicle is driven in a manner dangerous to public life.
Where a person does such an offence he is punished as per the provisions of Section 184 of the Act.

5 of 'culpable rashness' and 'culpable negligence' into consideration in cases of road accidents.

'Culpable rashness' is acting with the consciousness that mischievous and illegal consequences may follow but with the hope that they will not and often with the belief that the actor has taken sufficient precautions to prevent their happen
The imputability arises from acting despite consciousness (luxuria).

'Culpable negligence' is acting without the consciousness that the illegal and mischievous effect will follow, but in circumstances which show that the actor has not exercised the caution incumbent upon him and that if he had, he would have
The imputability arises from the neglect of civic duty of circumspection.
In such a case the mere fact of accident is prima facie evidence of such negligence.

This maxim suggests that on the circumstances of a given case the res speaks and is eloquent because the facts stand unexplained, with the result that the natural and reasonable inference from the facts, not a conjectural inference, shows t
13. The accident was caused during day time, at 08:00AM in month of September, on left side of the road and victim child was crushed under front left wheel of the truck driven by the accused.
The accident could not have happened except by rash or negligent driving of the accused.
PW1 deposed that appellant was driving his truck in a zigzag manner and at a fast speed, and, there is no reason to disbelieve his version.

Although, IO did not record statement of any other public witness,
who apprehended appellant at the spot, the deposition of PW1 is detailed, lucid and consistent; it withstood the test of cross-examination and is corroborated by other evide
Ld. Trial Court rightly relied upon the testimony of PW1 Ajay Kumar Rai to convict the appellant.
The appellant led no evidence in defence and gave an untenable and vacuous reply in statement U/s. 313 CrPC that his truck was stationed and he was sleeping on its roof.
Another vehicle had hit the deceased and fled from the spot, whereas, he was falsely implicated in present case.
14. In conclusion, it is observed that the impugned judgment dated 16/12/2017 is well reasoned and is based on correct appreciation of facts and evidence.
The appellant was rightly convicted for offence U/s. 279/304A IPC.
There is no substance in appeal and, so far as it impugns the judgment of conviction, it stands dismissed.
The issue of sentence shall be considered on completion of due procedure.
